title: 2010年考研英语一 Part B · 段落排序

sentences: Directions ; For questions 41-45, choose the most suitable paragraphs from the list A-G and fill them into the numbered boxes to form a coherent text.
Paragraph E has been correctly placed.
There is one paragraph which does not fit in with the text.
Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1.
(10 points)
translations: 说明；对于41-45题，从列表A-G中选择最合适的段落，并将它们填入编号的方框中，以形成连贯的文本。
段落E已被正确放置。
有一个段落不适合该文本。
在答题卡1上标记你的答案。

sentences: [A] The first and more important is the consumer’s growing preference for eating out: the consumption of food and drink in places other than homes has risen from about 32 percent of total consumption in 1995 to 35 percent in 2000 and is expected to approach 38 percent by 2005.
This development is boosting wholesale demand from the food service segment by 4 to 5 percent a year across Europe, compared with growth in retail demand of 1 to 2 percent.
Meanwhile, as the recession is looming large, people are getting anxious.
They tend to keep a tighter hold on their purse and consider eating at home a realistic alternative.
translations: [A] 第一个也是更重要的因素是消费者越来越倾向于外出就餐：在家庭以外的地方食品和饮料的消费从1995年占总消费的约32%上升到2000年的35%，预计到2005年将接近38%。
这一发展正在推动整个欧洲食品服务部门的批发需求每年增长4%到5%，而零售需求的增长仅为1%到2%。
与此同时，随着经济衰退的逼近，人们变得焦虑。
他们倾向于更紧地捂住钱包，并认为在家吃饭是一个现实的选择。

sentences: [B] Retail sales of food and drink in Europe’s largest markets are at a standstill, leaving European grocery retailers hungry for opportunities to grow.
Most leading retailers have already tried e-commerce, with limited success, and expansion abroad.
But almost all have ignored the big, profitable opportunity in their own backyard: the wholesale food and drink trade, which appears to be just the kind of market retailers need.
translations: [B] 欧洲最大市场的食品和饮料零售销售停滞不前，使得欧洲杂货零售商渴望增长机会。
大多数领先零售商已经尝试过电子商务，但成功有限，以及海外扩张。
但几乎所有人都忽略了自家后院中巨大且有利可图的机会：食品和饮料批发贸易，这似乎正是零售商所需的市场类型。

sentences: [C] Will such variations bring about a change in the overall structure of the food and drink market?
Definitely not.
The functioning of the market is based on flexible trends dominated by potential buyers.
In other words, it is up to the buyer, rather than the seller, to decide what to buy.
At any rate, this change will ultimately be acclaimed by an ever-growing number of both domestic and international consumers, regardless of how long the current consumer pattern will take hold.
translations: [C] 这些变化会带来食品和饮料市场整体结构的变化吗？
绝对不会。
市场的运作基于由潜在买家主导的灵活趋势。
换句话说，决定购买什么的是买家，而不是卖家。
无论如何，这一变化最终将受到越来越多的国内和国际消费者的欢迎，无论当前的消费模式能持续多久。

sentences: [D] All in all, this clearly seems to be a market in which big retailers could profitably apply their gigantic scale, existing infrastructure, and proven skills in the management of product ranges, logistics, and marketing intelligence.
Retailers that master the intricacies of wholesaling in Europe may well expect to rake in substantial profits thereby.
At least, that is how it looks as a whole.

Closer inspection reveals important differences among the biggest national markets, especially in their customer segments and wholesale structures, as well as the competitive dynamics of individual food and drink categories.
Big retailers must understand these differences before they can identify the segments of European wholesaling in which their particular abilities might unseat smaller but entrenched competitors.
New skills and unfamiliar business models are needed too.
translations: [D] 总而言之，这显然是一个大零售商可以有利可图地运用其巨大规模、现有基础设施以及在产品系列、物流和营销情报管理方面成熟技能的市场。
掌握欧洲批发业务复杂细节的零售商很可能期望借此获得可观的利润。
至少，整体上看是这样。
更仔细的观察揭示了最大的国家市场之间的重要差异，尤其是在其客户细分和批发结构，以及各个食品和饮料类别的竞争动态方面。
大零售商必须了解这些差异，才能确定欧洲批发业务中哪些细分市场可能让其特定能力取代规模较小但根深蒂固的竞争对手。
还需要新的技能和不熟悉的商业模式。

sentences: [E] Despite variations in detail, wholesale markets in the countries that have been closely examined—France, Germany, Italy and Spain—are made out of the same building blocks.

Demand comes mainly from two sources: independent mom-and-pop grocery stores which, unlike large retail chains, are too small to buy straight from producers, and food service operators that cater to consumers when they don’t eat at home.
Such food service operators range from snack machines to large institutional catering ventures, but most of these businesses are known in the trade as “horeca” ; hotels, restaurants, and cafés.
Overall, Europe’s wholesale market for food and drink is growing at the same sluggish pace as the retail market, but the figures, when added together, mask two opposing trends.
translations: [E] 尽管细节有所不同，但经过仔细考察的国家——法国、德国、意大利和西班牙——的批发市场是由相同的构建块组成的。
需求主要来自两个来源：独立的夫妻杂货店，与大型零售连锁店不同，它们太小而无法直接从生产商购买，以及为消费者不在家吃饭时提供服务的食品服务运营商。
此类食品服务运营商范围从零食机到大型机构餐饮企业，但大多数这些企业在业内被称为“horeca”；酒店、餐厅和咖啡馆。
总体而言，欧洲的食品和饮料批发市场正以与零售市场同样缓慢的速度增长，但将这些数字加在一起，掩盖了两种相反的趋势。

sentences: [F] For example, wholesale food and drink sales came to $268 billion in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom in 2000—more than 40 percent of retail sales.

Moreover, average overall margins are higher in wholesale than in retail; wholesale demand from the food service sector is growing quickly as more Europeans eat out more often; and changes in the competitive dynamics of this fragmented industry are at last making it feasible for wholesalers to consolidate.
translations: [F] 例如，2000年法国、德国、意大利、西班牙和英国的食品和饮料批发销售额达到2680亿美元——超过零售销售额的40%。
此外，批发的平均总体利润率高于零售；随着更多欧洲人更频繁地外出就餐，食品服务部门的批发需求正在快速增长；这个分散行业的竞争动态变化终于使批发商整合成为可能。

sentences: [G] However, none of these requirements should deter large retailers (and even some large food producers and existing wholesalers) from trying their hand, for those that master the intricacies of wholesaling in Europe stand to reap considerable gains.
translations: [G] 然而，这些要求都不应阻止大型零售商（甚至一些大型食品生产商和现有批发商）尝试，因为那些掌握欧洲批发业务复杂细节的人有望获得可观的收益。
